title: Structured auth event log with zero secret leakage
description: Every material auth event emits one structured log entry: sign-in requested, magic link minted, magic link sent, magic link consumed, session issued, session refreshed, session invalidated, session revoked, rate-limit tripped, adapter-send failed. Each entry carries at minimum an event name, a UTC timestamp, an outcome, and where applicable a principal id and a request id. Token secrets, session handles, and email-delivery-provider api keys never appear in any field of any log entry.
rationale: An unlogged auth surface is a black box the first time it misfires; a logged auth surface that quotes tokens is the same black box plus a smoking gun in the log store. Naming the event set and forbidding secret quoting means the log is useful in an incident without becoming an incident itself.
